b2-colombiaperiferias-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Founded Cartagena
b2-colombiaperiferias-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Cartagena, and he asks what the narrator said about the city.
b2-colombiaperiferias-01.prompt: Tell Carlos who founded Cartagena and when.
cues: Say that the city was founded
Say by whom and in which year
b2-colombiaperiferias-01.target: Cartagena fue fundada en 1533 por Pedro de Heredia.
b2-colombiaperiferias-01.english: Cartagena was founded in 1533 by Pedro de Heredia.
b2-colombiaperiferias-01.canDo: I can say who founded or built something with *ser* + past participle.

b2-colombiaperiferias-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Why So Few Roads
b2-colombiaperiferias-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read an article about the Pacific coast of Colombia, and Meg asks how people travel there.
b2-colombiaperiferias-02.prompt: Tell Meg why there are few roads on the Pacific coast.
cues: Give the reason with a formal connector
Say that there are few roads
b2-colombiaperiferias-02.target: Debido a la lluvia y a la selva, hay pocas carreteras en el Pacífico.
b2-colombiaperiferias-02.english: Because of the rain and the forest, there are few roads on the Pacific coast.
b2-colombiaperiferias-02.canDo: I can give a cause with *debido a* or *a raíz de* followed by a noun.

b2-colombiaperiferias-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Rule for Collective Lands
b2-colombiaperiferias-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you read about Law 70 of 1993 for a talk you are planning.
b2-colombiaperiferias-03.prompt: Say what the law says about the collective lands, in the formal register of a law.
cues: Say that the lands cannot be sold
b2-colombiaperiferias-03.target: Las tierras colectivas no podrán venderse.
b2-colombiaperiferias-03.english: The collective lands may not be sold.
b2-colombiaperiferias-03.canDo: I can turn an everyday request into a formal rule with *todo aquel que*, the future and *se*.

b2-colombiaperiferias-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Commission Said
b2-colombiaperiferias-04.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a news report about the Truth Commission, and he asks what it said about the conflict.
b2-colombiaperiferias-04.prompt: Tell Carlos what the Commission said in its 2022 report.
cues: Say what the conflict had left behind
b2-colombiaperiferias-04.target: La Comisión dijo en su informe que el conflicto había dejado cientos de miles de muertos.
b2-colombiaperiferias-04.english: The Commission said in its report that the conflict had left hundreds of thousands dead.
b2-colombiaperiferias-04.canDo: I can report what someone said with *dijo que* and the right tense shift.

b2-colombiaperiferias-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Park Closed to Tourists
b2-colombiaperiferias-05.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read an article about Chiribiquete, and Meg asks whether tourists can visit the park.
b2-colombiaperiferias-05.prompt: Tell Meg that the park is closed, and that people still know its paintings.
cues: Say that the park is closed to tourists
Say that many people still know the paintings
b2-colombiaperiferias-05.target: Aun cuando el parque está cerrado a los turistas, muchas personas conocen sus pinturas.
b2-colombiaperiferias-05.english: Even though the park is closed to tourists, many people know its paintings.
b2-colombiaperiferias-05.canDo: I can use *aun cuando* with the subjunctive for a possibility and with the indicative for a fact.

b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Palenque and UNESCO
b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you remember from your reading about Colombia.
b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.prompt: Say what UNESCO did for Palenque in 2005.
b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.target: Palenque fue reconocido por la UNESCO en 2005.
b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.english: Palenque was recognised by UNESCO in 2005.
b2-colombiaperiferias-consolidation.canDo: I can say who founded, built or recognised something with *ser* + past participle.
